Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a diffuse reticulonodular pattern involving both lungs, and the blunting of the costophrenic angles (particularly on the left) indicates bilateral pleural effusions. This combination of diffuse interstitial markings and fluid is most consistent with an interstitial lung disease or lymphangitic spread, distinguishing it from options describing upper-lobe predominance (LCH), absence of pattern (pneumonia), or isolated lower-lobe edema without the noted diffuse nodularity.
